text: So when I joined, we were about 10-ish folks, about eight engineers, and in three months, we built a competitor to Amex. Six months after that, we built a competitor to Expensify, both publicly traded companies. We hit a hundred million in annual revenue.
speaker: Geoff Charles
context: Lenny asks for concrete examples of what velocity actually looks like at Ramp beyond just saying they move fast. Geoff provides specific examples of how small teams at Ramp built competitors to major publicly traded companies in extremely short timeframes. He explains how they built products that compete with American Express and Expensify with minimal team sizes, and how they expanded into accounts payable with just a 5-person team that created a product processing billions of dollars annually.
text_ko: 제가 합류했을 때, 팀이 한 10명 정도였고, 그 중 8명이 엔지니어였어요. 3개월 만에 Amex의 경쟁 제품을 만들었고, 그로부터 6개월 후에는 Expensify의 경쟁 제품도 만들었죠. 두 회사 모두 상장된 회사인데, 우리는 연매출 1억 달러를 달성했어요. 그 당시 R&D 부서에는 50명도 안 되고, 엔지니어는 4명도 안 됐고 PM은 3명이었어요. 그리고 나서 우리는 외상 매출금(accounts payable) 쪽으로 확장을 시작했어요. 그때 엔지니어 3명, 디자이너 1명, PM 1명으로 3개월 만에 대박을 쳤죠. 그 제품은 연간 수십억 달러를 움직이고 있어요.
text_zh: 我刚加入的时候，团队大概就10个人左右，8个工程师。三个月内，我们就做出了一个能跟美国运通(Amex)竞争的产品。又过了六个月，我们又搞出了一个跟Expensify竞争的产品，这俩都是上市公司啊。我们做到了年收入一个亿美金。那时候我们整个研发部门还不到50个人，工程师不到4个，产品经理3个。后来我们开始拓展应付账款(accounts payable)业务，就3个工程师，1个设计师，1个产品经理，三个月时间，结果做得特别成功。这个产品现在一年能跑几十亿美金的流水。
text_es: Entonces cuando me uní, éramos como 10 personas, unos ocho ingenieros, y en tres meses armamos un competidor de Amex. Seis meses después, creamos un competidor de Expensify, ambas empresas que cotizan en bolsa. Llegamos a cien millones en ingresos anuales. Creo que en ese momento éramos menos de 50 en total en el departamento de I+D, menos de cuatro ingenieros y tres PMs. Y entonces empezamos a expandirnos a cuentas por pagar. Fueron tres ingenieros, un diseñador, un PM, tres meses, y la pegaron fuera del estadio. Y ese producto está moviendo miles de millones de dólares al año.
key_sentence: we built a competitor to Amex.
original_text: So when I joined, we were about 10-ish folks, about eight engineers, and in three months, we built a competitor to Amex. Six months after that, we built a competitor to Expensify, both publicly traded companies. We hit a hundred million in annual revenue. I think we were under at that point, 50 total in the R&D department, less than four engineers and three PMs. And then we started expanding into accounts payable. It was three engineers, one designer, one PM three months, and they hit out of the park. And that product is moving in billions of dollars a year.

vocabulary.definition: An individual or organization that competes against others in the same market or industry.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, identifying competitors is crucial for strategic planning, market analysis, and positioning products or services effectively.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'competitor' typically refers to direct rivals, it can also encompass indirect competitors that offer alternative solutions.

vocabulary.definition: The total income generated by a company from its business activities over the course of a year, before any expenses are deducted.
vocabulary.businessContext: Annual revenue is a key performance indicator used by stakeholders to assess a company's financial health and growth potential.
vocabulary.nuance: While often used interchangeably with 'sales,' annual revenue specifically refers to the total income, which may include other sources beyond direct sales.

vocabulary.definition: In a business context, velocity refers to the speed at which a company can deliver products or services to the market or the rate of growth in sales or revenue.
vocabulary.businessContext: Understanding velocity helps businesses optimize their operations, improve time-to-market, and enhance customer satisfaction.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'velocity' often implies speed, it can also encompass the efficiency of processes and the ability to adapt to market changes.

vocabulary.definition: Referring to a company whose shares are available for purchase by the general public on a stock exchange.
vocabulary.businessContext: Publicly traded companies are subject to regulatory scrutiny and must disclose financial information, making them more transparent to investors.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'publicly traded' implies a level of maturity and credibility, often associated with larger firms, but it can also suggest vulnerability to market fluctuations.

text: There are very few people who are able to execute extremely well in more than one thing, and it's especially true for individual contributors.
speaker: Geoff Charles
context: Lenny asks Geoff to explain what 'single-threaded teams' means in practice, as this was mentioned as a key ingredient for moving fast at Ramp. Geoff clarifies that single-threaded means each person has literally one goal or 'thread' they focus on when they wake up each morning. He explains this requires actively removing all other distractions, tasks, research, or processes that don't directly contribute to that single goal.
text_ko: 여러 분야에서 아주 뛰어나게 실행할 수 있는 사람은 거의 없고, 특히 개인 기여자(individual contributors)에게는 더 그래요. 제가 '한 가지에만 집중하는(single-threaded)'이라고 말할 때는, 아침에 일어나서 오직 하나의 목표, 하나의 실무에만 집중한다는 뜻이에요. 그리고 그런 상태를 만들려면, 기본적으로 그들이 하라고 요청받는 다른 모든 일을 제거해야 해요 — 연구(research)이든 생산 엔지니어링(production engineering)이든, 그 단일 목표와 상관없는 어떤 업무나 프로세스도요.
text_zh: 能够在多个领域都做得特别出色的人真的很少，对于一线员工来说更是如此。我说的"单线程(single threaded)"就是指他们每天早上醒来只专注一个目标、一条线。要做到这一点，你基本上得把他们手上其他所有的活儿都拿掉，让他们就盯着这一件事，不管是什么研究工作、生产工程，还是跟这个核心目标无关的流程，统统都得清理掉。
text_es: Hay muy poca gente que puede ejecutar súper bien en más de una cosa a la vez, y esto es especialmente cierto para los colaboradores individuales. Cuando digo "single threaded" me refiero a que solo hay un objetivo, un hilo conductor, en el que se enfocan cuando se levantan por las mañanas. Y para lograr eso, básicamente necesitas quitarles todo lo demás que les estés pidiendo que hagan para que se concentren únicamente en esa cosa - ya sea cualquier tipo de investigación, ingeniería de producción, o cualquier proceso que esté fuera de ese objetivo único.
key_sentence: There are very few people who are able to execute extremely well in more than one thing.
original_text: There are very few people who are able to execute extremely well in more than one thing, and it's especially true for individual contributors. And so what I mean by single threaded is there's only one goal, one thread, that they're waking up in the morning to focus on. And in order to remove that, you basically need to remove anything else that they're being asked to do to just focus on that thing, whether it's any type of research or any type of production engineering or any type of process that's outside of that single goal.

vocabulary.definition: To carry out or put into effect a plan, order, or course of action.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, executing refers to the implementation of strategies, projects, or tasks to achieve specific objectives.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'execute' often implies efficiency and precision, it can also suggest a lack of creativity if used in contexts that require innovation.

vocabulary.definition: Employees who contribute to a project or organization primarily through their specialized skills and expertise, rather than through managerial or supervisory roles.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, individual contributors are often crucial for driving innovation and delivering results without the responsibilities of team leadership.
vocabulary.nuance: The term emphasizes the value of specialized skills and can sometimes imply a lack of authority or decision-making power compared to management roles.

vocabulary.definition: Referring to a process or task that is focused on a single line of execution or a singular focus, often implying a lack of multitasking.
vocabulary.businessContext: In project management and software development, a single-threaded approach can enhance focus and efficiency by prioritizing one task at a time.
vocabulary.nuance: While single-threaded can imply depth of focus, it may also suggest limitations in adaptability or responsiveness to multiple demands.

vocabulary.definition: An essential component or factor that is crucial for achieving a desired outcome or success.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business strategy, identifying the key ingredients for success can help organizations focus their efforts on what truly drives results.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase often conveys a sense of importance and can be used to highlight both tangible and intangible factors in a business context.

text: The first thing is we have market comparables, which is very exciting for us.
speaker: Geoff Charles
context: Lenny asks how Ramp finds the balance between setting ambitious goals versus impossible goals, referencing how other companies like Airbnb are known for very lofty targets. Geoff explains that having market comparables - existing publicly traded competitors like Bill.com and Expensify - makes ambitious goals feel more achievable and helps de-risk business decisions. He notes they can point to these successful companies as proof that large markets exist for their products.
text_ko: 우선 우리에겐 시장 비교 자료(market comparables)가 있다는 것만 해도 정말 고무적이에요. Bill.com이나 Expensify는 상장사고 Concur나 Coupa 같은 회사들도 모두 큰 플레이어라서 오히려 자극이 되고 우리가 내리는 여러 사업 결정의 리스크를 상당히 줄여줘요(de-risk). 그건 기존 시장(existing markets)에 해당해요. 또 저희는 시장을 만들어내기도 했어요. 스펜드 매니지먼트(spend management)라는 시장은 저희와 다른 경쟁사들이 뛰어들기 전부터 이미 실제로 존재하던 시장이었어요.
text_zh: 首先呢，我们有市场对标公司，这对我们来说特别振奋人心。你看像Bill.com，他们是上市公司，还有Expensify也上市了，或者Concur、Coupa这些，都是行业大玩家，真的很激励人，而且在很大程度上能降低我们做商业决策的风险。这些都是现有市场。我们也有能力去创造市场。支出管理(spend management)在我们和其他竞争对手进入之前，其实就已经是一个实实在在的市场了。
text_es: Lo primero es que tenemos comparables del mercado (market comparables), lo cual es súper emocionante para nosotros. Entonces cuando miras a Bill.com, que cotiza en bolsa, Expensify, que también cotiza públicamente, o Concur o Coupa, todos estos son jugadores grandes que realmente te motivan y en gran medida reducen el riesgo de las decisiones de negocio que estás tomando. Esos son mercados que ya existen. También hemos podido crear mercados. La gestión de gastos (spend management) ya era un mercado real antes de que nosotros y otros competidores nos metiéramos.
key_sentence: we have market comparables, which is very exciting for us.
original_text: The first thing is we have market comparables, which is very exciting for us. So when you look at Bill.com, they're a publicly traded company, Expensify, publicly traded, or Concur or Coupa, these are all large players that are actually very motivating and largely de-risk some of the business decisions you're making. That's existing markets. We've also been able to create markets. Spend management was an actual market before we and other competitors jump into it.

vocabulary.definition: Market comparables are benchmarks derived from the performance or valuation of similar companies or assets within a specific market. They are used to assess the relative value of a business or investment.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and finance, market comparables are often utilized during valuation processes, mergers and acquisitions, or investment analyses to provide a reference point for pricing or performance expectations.
vocabulary.nuance: The term implies a level of analysis and comparison that is essential for informed decision-making, but it may not capture unique factors affecting individual companies.

vocabulary.definition: Ambitious goals are objectives that are challenging and require significant effort and resources to achieve. They often push the boundaries of what is currently possible.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, ambitious goals are set to inspire teams and drive innovation, often leading to higher performance and growth, but they also carry risks of overreach.
vocabulary.nuance: While ambitious goals can motivate and foster a culture of excellence, they may also lead to stress and burnout if perceived as unattainable.

vocabulary.definition: Lofty targets refer to high and often idealistic objectives that organizations aim to achieve, typically requiring extraordinary effort and commitment.
vocabulary.businessContext: In corporate strategy, lofty targets are often set to drive growth and innovation, serving as a rallying point for teams to strive towards, albeit with the understanding that they may be difficult to reach.
vocabulary.nuance: The term carries a positive connotation of ambition, but it can also imply a disconnect from practical realities if not grounded in achievable steps.

vocabulary.definition: Exciting describes something that generates enthusiasm, interest, or eagerness, often due to its novelty or potential impact.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, the term is frequently used to describe new products, innovations, or market opportunities that have the potential to engage customers or drive growth.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'exciting' conveys a positive emotional response, it should be used judiciously to avoid overstating the significance of a situation or development.

text: And oftentimes, more junior leaders, and I was certainly in that camp earlier on, kept focusing on the solutions and debating the right solution when in fact you should really be debating upstream of that.
speaker: Geoff Charles
context: Lenny asks how Ramp operationalizes 'context over control' - empowering product teams without micromanaging them. Geoff explains that successful empowerment starts with alignment on goals, hypotheses, and data interpretation rather than debating specific solutions. He shares that junior leaders often make the mistake of focusing downstream on solutions when they should be focusing upstream on understanding the problem, data, and objectives first.
text_ko: 종종 주니어 리더들(junior leaders)은—저도 예전엔 그랬어요—해결책에만 계속 집착해서 어떤 해결책이 옳은지 논쟁하곤 해요. 그런데 사실은 그보다 앞선 단계, 즉 상위 단계(upstream)에서 논의해야 해요. 데이터 해석(interpretation of data)을 두고 토론하고, 가설(hypotheses)이나 실제로 무슨 일이 일어나고 있는지에 대한 다양한 아이디어들을 검토하거나, 때로는 목표 자체(goals)를 다시 논의해야 해요.
text_zh: 很多时候，那些资历比较浅的领导者，我以前也是这样，总是盯着解决方案不放，老在那儿争论哪个方案更好。其实你应该往前推一步，应该争论的是对数据的理解，应该争论各种假设和想法——到底发生了什么，或者干脆争论目标本身对不对。
text_es: Y muchas veces, los líderes más junior, y yo claramente estaba en ese grupo al principio, se la pasaban enfocándose en las soluciones y discutiendo cuál era la solución correcta, cuando en realidad deberían estar debatiendo mucho antes de llegar ahí. Deberían estar debatiendo cómo interpretan los datos, deberían estar debatiendo las hipótesis y las diferentes ideas que tienen sobre qué está pasando realmente, o deberían estar debatiendo los objetivos mismos.
key_sentence: Debating the hypotheses is more important than focusing on solutions upstream of that.
original_text: And oftentimes, more junior leaders, and I was certainly in that camp earlier on, kept focusing on the solutions and debating the right solution when in fact you should really be debating upstream of that. You should be debating the interpretation of data, you should be debating the hypotheses and the different ideas that you have there as to what's really going on or you should be debating the goals themselves.

vocabulary.definition: The act of discussing or arguing about a particular topic or issue, often with the intention of reaching a conclusion or decision.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, debating is crucial during decision-making processes, where teams evaluate different strategies or solutions to identify the most effective approach.
vocabulary.nuance: While debating can foster critical thinking and innovation, excessive debating without action can lead to analysis paralysis.

vocabulary.definition: Referring to the earlier stages in a process or supply chain, where foundational decisions and actions are made that influence subsequent outcomes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, thinking upstream involves addressing root causes and strategic planning before executing specific solutions, ensuring that the right problems are tackled first.
vocabulary.nuance: Using 'upstream' emphasizes a proactive approach to problem-solving, contrasting with reactive measures that address issues only after they arise.

vocabulary.definition: The process of ensuring that all stakeholders, teams, or elements are working towards the same goals and objectives, fostering coherence and unity.
vocabulary.businessContext: In organizations, alignment is essential for effective collaboration and strategic execution, as it helps to synchronize efforts across different departments or teams.
vocabulary.nuance: While alignment is generally positive, it can sometimes imply conformity at the expense of creativity, so it’s important to balance alignment with individual input.

vocabulary.definition: The process of granting individuals or teams the authority, confidence, and resources to make decisions and take actions independently.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, empowerment is key to fostering a culture of innovation and accountability, enabling employees to contribute more effectively to organizational goals.
vocabulary.nuance: Empowerment carries a positive connotation of trust and autonomy, but it requires a supportive environment to be effective; otherwise, it can lead to confusion and lack of direction.

text: We don't have a bug backlog. We fix every bug once they're surfaced almost. So it's part of the production engineer's job really just to fix those things.
speaker: Geoff Charles
context: Lenny asks how teams should balance fixing quality issues and bugs versus hitting their main KPIs and goals. Geoff explains Ramp's approach to maintaining quality while moving fast - they don't maintain a traditional bug backlog but instead fix every bug immediately when it's discovered. He describes how they track customer confusion through support tickets as a key quality metric, and teams must stop shipping new features if this metric gets elevated.
text_ko: 우리는 버그 백로그(bug backlog)가 없어요. 버그가 발견되면 거의 바로 고쳐요. 그래서 그런 것들을 고치는 건 사실 프로덕션 엔지니어(production engineer)의 업무 중 하나예요. 사용자 경험 개선(user experience improvements)처럼 미묘한 부분으로 가면, 제가 실제로 보는 지표는 고객이 혼란스러워해서 들어오는 지원 티켓(support tickets)의 수예요.
text_zh: 我们不会积压bug。基本上一发现问题就马上修，这其实就是生产工程师的活儿。但涉及到一些细节，比如用户体验优化这块，我主要看的指标就是有多少客服工单(support tickets)是因为用户搞不清楚操作才提交的。
text_es: No tenemos una acumulación de errores pendientes. Arreglamos casi todos los bugs en cuanto salen a la luz. Así que es parte del trabajo del ingeniero de producción simplemente solucionar esas cosas. Creo que donde entramos en matices, como mejoras en la experiencia del usuario (user experience), la métrica que realmente reviso es cuántos tickets de soporte nos llegan porque un cliente se confundió.
key_sentence: We don't have a bug backlog; we fix every bug once surfaced.
original_text: We don't have a bug backlog. We fix every bug once they're surfaced almost. So it's part of the production engineer's job really just to fix those things. I think where we get to nuances, like user experience improvements, the metric there that I really look at is how many support tickets come in that were due to a customer being confused.

vocabulary.definition: A backlog refers to an accumulation of tasks, requests, or issues that have not yet been addressed or completed. It often indicates a delay in processing or fulfilling these items.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, a backlog can arise in project management, software development, or customer service, where tasks are queued for resolution or action.
vocabulary.nuance: While a backlog can indicate inefficiency, it may also suggest a high demand for services or products, depending on the context.

vocabulary.definition: A production engineer is a professional responsible for overseeing and optimizing the production process in manufacturing or technology settings, ensuring efficiency and quality in output.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech startups, production engineers play a crucial role in managing the development and deployment of software products, often focusing on troubleshooting and resolving issues that arise during production.
vocabulary.nuance: The term may imply a focus on practical application and problem-solving within the production environment, distinguishing it from more theoretical engineering roles.

vocabulary.definition: Quality issues refer to problems or defects that affect the performance, reliability, or overall standard of a product or service. These issues can arise during production, testing, or after delivery.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech settings, addressing quality issues is critical for maintaining customer satisfaction and compliance with industry standards, often leading to additional testing or revisions.
vocabulary.nuance: The term carries a negative connotation, suggesting a failure to meet expected standards, and is often used in discussions about product improvements and customer feedback.

vocabulary.definition: Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) are measurable values that demonstrate how effectively an organization is achieving its key business objectives. They are used to evaluate success at reaching targets.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, KPIs are essential for tracking progress, making informed decisions, and aligning team efforts with strategic goals.
vocabulary.nuance: The term is often used in a formal context, and while it indicates measurable success, it can also imply a focus on quantitative metrics over qualitative aspects.

text: Behind Ramp's velocity is a lot less the culture that I try to amplify, but a lot more the quality of the engineering and design talent candidly. And so I'm just standing really on their shoulders here.
speaker: Geoff Charles
context: Lenny mentions that after their post about Ramp's approach, many CEOs started pressuring their PMs to move faster like Ramp, and asks for advice for PMs facing this pressure. Geoff clarifies that Ramp's velocity comes primarily from having exceptional engineering and design talent rather than just culture. He emphasizes that leaders must first invest in R&D as a priority, pay competitive rates, hire top talent, and build a strong engineering brand that attracts people who want to be empowered.
text_ko: Ramp의 속도 뒤에는 제가 강조하려는 문화보다 솔직히 말해서 엔지니어링과 디자인 인재의 품질이 훨씬 더 중요해요. 그래서 저는 그들의 어깨 위에 서 있는 거죠. 첫 번째 조언은 위에서부터 R&D에 대한 투자가 1급 시민으로 이루어지도록 해야 한다는 거예요. 즉, 좋은 인재를 채용하고, 엔지니어링과 기술 브랜드에 집중하며, 그곳에서 일하고 싶어 하는 사람들을 끌어들이는 것이죠. 그들이 권한을 부여받고 싶어 하니까요.
text_zh: Ramp能发展这么快，说实话主要不是因为我推动的企业文化，更多的是因为我们工程和设计团队的质量真的很高。我其实就是站在他们肩膀上而已。所以我的第一个建议就是，从上到下一定要把研发(R&D)当成头等大事来投资，该花的钱不能省，要招最好的人，要好好打造你的工程和技术品牌，要让那些真正想发挥才能的人愿意来你这里工作。
text_es: Detrás de la velocidad de Ramp hay mucho menos de la cultura que trato de impulsar, y mucho más de la calidad del talento en ingeniería y diseño, para ser honesto. Yo simplemente me apoyo en sus hombros aquí. Entonces mi primer consejo es asegurarte de que desde arriba haya una inversión en I+D como ciudadano de primera clase - que pagues bien en el mercado premium, que contrates a los mejores, que te enfoques en tu marca de ingeniería y tecnología, que traigas gente que quiera trabajar ahí porque quieren sentirse empoderados.
key_sentence: Behind Ramp's velocity is a lot less the culture that I try to amplify, but a lot more the quality of the engineering and design talent candidly.
original_text: Behind Ramp's velocity is a lot less the culture that I try to amplify, but a lot more the quality of the engineering and design talent candidly. And so I'm just standing really on their shoulders here. And so advice number one is ensure that from the top down there's an investment in R&D as a first-class citizen that you're paying upmarket, that you're hiring the best, that you're focusing on your engineering and tech brand, that you're bringing people who want to work there because they want to be empowered.

vocabulary.definition: Velocity refers to the speed of something in a given direction, often used to describe the rate of progress or change in a particular context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, velocity often pertains to the speed at which a team can deliver products or services, particularly in agile methodologies where rapid iteration is crucial.
vocabulary.nuance: While velocity generally implies speed, in a business context, it also encompasses the effectiveness and efficiency of processes, making it more than just a measure of time.

vocabulary.definition: To amplify means to increase the volume, intensity, or significance of something, often by adding more resources or support.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, amplifying can refer to enhancing a brand's message, increasing market reach, or boosting team morale through strategic initiatives.
vocabulary.nuance: Amplify carries a connotation of not just increasing quantity but also enhancing quality or impact, making it suitable for contexts where improvement is desired.

vocabulary.definition: Engineering is the application of scientific and mathematical principles to design, build, and analyze structures, systems, and processes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, engineering is crucial for developing software and hardware products, where skilled engineers translate ideas into functional solutions.
vocabulary.nuance: While engineering typically refers to technical disciplines, it can also imply problem-solving and innovation, making it relevant in various business discussions.

vocabulary.definition: Candidly means speaking in an honest and straightforward manner, without any pretense or deceit.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business communications, being candid can foster transparency and trust, especially during feedback sessions or discussions about challenges and opportunities.
vocabulary.nuance: Candidly implies a level of openness that may sometimes be uncomfortable, but is often necessary for genuine dialogue and problem-solving.

text: I think the debate around working hard and burnout misses a key point, which is all about how much impact and how good you feel about the work that you're doing.
speaker: Geoff Charles
context: Lenny asks about burnout concerns given Ramp's intense focus on velocity and constant shipping. Geoff argues that the typical debate about working hard versus burnout misses a crucial point - burnout is more about lack of impact and meaningful progress than about working long hours. He shares that his personal experience with burnout occurred during periods of low velocity when he felt he was putting effort into work that wasn't actually moving the needle or creating meaningful outcomes.
text_ko: 열심히 일하는 것과 번아웃에 대한 논의는 중요한 한 가지를 놓치고 있는 것 같아요. 그건 바로 당신이 하는 일이 얼마나 임팩트(impact)가 있는지, 그리고 그 일에 대해 얼마나 만족감이나 보람을 느끼는지예요. 제 경우 번아웃을 느꼈을 때는 사실 진행 속도(velocity)가 가장 낮았을 때였어요. 많은 노력을 들이고 있다고 느꼈는데도 정작 일이 앞으로 나아가지 않을 때였죠.
text_zh: 我觉得大家在讨论努力工作和职业倦怠的时候，漏掉了一个关键点，就是你的工作到底能产生多大影响，以及你对自己做的事情感觉怎么样。对我来说，我感到倦怠的时候，其实恰恰是我工作效率最低的时候。那时候我感觉自己明明很努力，但做的那些事情根本没什么进展。
text_es: Creo que todo el debate sobre trabajar duro y el agotamiento se pierde un punto clave, que tiene que ver con el impacto que generas y qué tan bien te sientes con el trabajo que estás haciendo. Y para mí, cuando me sentí quemado, en realidad fue justo cuando tenía menos velocidad. Pero era cuando sentía que le estaba metiendo un montón de esfuerzo a cosas que realmente no estaban avanzando.
key_sentence: The debate around burnout misses a key point about impact and moving the needle.
original_text: I think the debate around working hard and burnout misses a key point, which is all about how much impact and how good you feel about the work that you're doing. And I think that for me, when I felt burnout, it was actually at the time where I had the lowest amount of velocity. But it was when I felt like I was putting a lot of effort into things that weren't actually moving.

vocabulary.definition: The strong effect or influence that something has on a situation or person.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'impact' often refers to the measurable outcomes of a project or initiative, such as increased revenue or improved customer satisfaction.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'impact' can imply a positive effect, it can also refer to negative consequences, so context is important when using the term.

vocabulary.definition: A state of physical, emotional, and mental exhaustion caused by prolonged stress or overwork.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the workplace, burnout can lead to decreased productivity, increased absenteeism, and higher turnover rates, making it a critical issue for management.
vocabulary.nuance: Burnout is often associated with chronic stress and can be more severe than simple fatigue, indicating a need for systemic changes rather than individual solutions.

vocabulary.definition: Extremely important or essential, especially in determining the outcome of a situation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business strategy, identifying crucial factors can help prioritize resources and efforts to achieve success.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'crucial' implies high importance, it can also suggest a sense of urgency, making it more impactful than simply 'important.'

vocabulary.definition: The speed at which something moves or operates, often used to describe the rate of progress in a given context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In agile project management, 'velocity' refers to the amount of work completed in a given timeframe, helping teams measure their efficiency and predict future performance.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'velocity' typically denotes speed, it can also imply a focus on the quality of progress, distinguishing it from mere rapidity.
